claim_updates.reason: Directional reversal persists under corrected implementation: per-task weighted recipe C2 TRUE (observed 0.333 > null 0.205, all 10 seeds TRUE, SD 0.0046) and canonical per-iteration recipe C2 FALSE (observed 0.333 < null 0.586, all 10 seeds FALSE, SD 0.0123) — recipe choice flips C2 direction (divergence 0.38), confirming reversal is NOT an artifact of unsorted-set/estimator bugs (F1 not triggered, F2 not triggered). However, quantitative reproduction of parent stored values fails: canonical null mean deviates 0.0424 from parent 0.5273 (exceeds B1 0.02 threshold), per-task weighted null mean deviates 0.07 from parent ~0.28 (exceeds NC2/F3 0.05 threshold). Frozen decision rule has no branch for MIXED outcome (reversal persists but NC2/F3 fail). Claim ceiling bounded to truncated-first-20 locatable sample (7 tasks deduped, 3 definitions, 1 Magento site), sorted(raw_roles), within-iteration agreement mean, frozen seeds. Does NOT establish SURVIVES_REVERSAL_PERSISTS as frozen (requires NC2/F3 pass), full-DOM ordering, cross-site invariance, 5-definition family agreement, or broader C-MEAS-VALID status. Density metric ordering is definition-dependent AND recipe-dependent.

product_action: No product promotion. Density metric ordering is definition-dependent (parent finding) AND recipe-dependent (this experiment): canonical recipe gives C2 FALSE (definitions disagree more than random), per-task weighted recipe gives C2 TRUE (definitions agree more than random). Product must pivot away from ordering-based density metrics entirely, or adopt a meta-analytic approach that bounds conclusions across recipes. The canonical per-iteration recipe remains the principled choice for C-MEAS-VALID (uniform application, controls for role preferences).
next_question: Does C2 FALSE (density ordering less stable than random role subsets) hold on full-DOM enumeration after the runtime lane removes the locatableSample cap at measure_fullpage_yield.py:89 — and does the per-task weighted recipe's C2 TRUE reversal also persist on full-DOM, confirming that recipe choice remains material at scale?
reason: The experiment resolves the key scientific question: the recipe reversal is genuine, not an implementation artifact. Under corrected implementation (sorted roles + direct estimator), the canonical per-iteration recipe reproduces C2 FALSE (observed 0.333 < null 0.586) and the per-task weighted recipe produces C2 TRUE (observed 0.333 > null 0.205) — recipe choice flips the C2 direction entirely (divergence 0.38). This is robust across all 10 frozen seeds (SD 0.0123 canonical, 0.0046 per-task). However, the frozen decision rule's SURVIVES_REVERSAL_PERSISTS requires NC2 (per-task null within 0.05 of 0.28) and F3 (deviation <0.05), both fail (deviation 0.07). The canonical null mean also deviates from parent (0.0424 > 0.02 threshold). The parent's stored values were affected by implementation bugs, but C2 directions are preserved. The audit's REVISE status is accepted: the decision rule gap (no MIXED branch) is a spec design failure, not an execution failure. The quantitative drift indicates implementation non-identity between parent and this run (definition/estimator drift not fully documented), but the directional scientific finding is robust. The claim ceiling is bounded to truncated-first-20; full-DOM re-run remains the critical next step once the substrate cap is removed.
